candidates.exact_span: There shall be no discharge of oils, scum, grease and other floating materials that would cause the formation of a visible sheen or visible deposits on the bottom or shoreline, or would damage or impair the normal growth, function or reproduction of human, animal, plant or aquatic life.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This is a qualitative prohibition rather than a numeric limit; interpretation of covered materials ('oils, scum, grease and other floating materials'), the causal trigger ('would cause'), and the alternative harm pathways (visible sheen/deposits vs. impairment of life) determines whether numeric compliance comparison is applicable (A) and how to classify monitoring periods that lack numeric results (C).

candidates.exact_span: Monitoring information shall be submitted quarterly. Each quarterly submittal shall include separate forms for each month of the reporting period.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'monitoring information' scope and whether separate monthly forms are required even during no-discharge months establishes the frequency and granularity of reporting obligations (B) and whether a missing monthly result reflects a documented no-discharge period, a conditional non-requirement, or inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Reporting periods shall end on the last day of the months March, June, September, and December.
candidates.computation_change_reason: These calendar quarter boundaries define which monitoring periods fall within Federal FY2025 and how submittals map to months; different readings of period boundaries change which obligations were applicable and which missing-evidence cases align to a required reporting window (B, C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee is required to submit regular quarterly reports as described above postmarked no later than the 28th day of the month following each reporting period.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The postmark deadline establishes when quarterly reporting was due; whether a given FY2025 quarter's report was timely, late, or absent affects determination of applicable reporting obligations (B) and whether missing data should be treated as unresolved required monitoring versus another documented state (C).

candidates.exact_span: Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) results shall be electronically reported to EPA per 40 CFR 127.16.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes electronic DMR submission as a binding reporting modality; interpretation of whether and when this requirement was operative determines applicable monitoring-reporting obligations for evaluated facilities (B).

candidates.exact_span: Until approved for Net DMR, the permittee shall request temporary or emergency waivers from electronic reporting.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the permittee was unapproved for NetDMR and whether a waiver was in effect changes whether the electronic reporting obligation applied as written or was modified, affecting evaluated monitoring obligations (B) and the evidentiary status of submissions that used an alternative pathway (C).

candidates.exact_span: If paper reporting is granted temporarily, the permittee shall submit the original DMR signed and certified as required by Part III.D.11 and all other reports required by Part III.D. to the EPA and copies to NMED as required (See Part III.D.IV of the permit ).
candidates.computation_change_reason: This conditional alternative reporting pathway, including cross-references to Part III.D certification and distribution requirements, determines what reporting was required when electronic submission was waived; interpretation of whether paper reporting was granted and which Part III.D provisions governed submissions affects obligation applicability (B) and whether available evidence satisfies the required reporting form (C).
